issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify addGuestStudents(int, String) (a method taking an int and a String reason), but the solution implements addGuestStudents with only a single int parameter. This parameter mismatch is structural: students will be instructed to implement a two-parameter method while the provided solution uses a different signature, which will cause test or usage mismatches and confusion.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signatures consistent. Update the solution (and template example implementation if present) to implement addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, String reason) so it matches the UML and problem description. The method body can add the new guest students to numberOfGuestStudents and optionally record or log the reason (even if unused) to satisfy the specified parameter list. Alternatively, if the second parameter is unnecessary, update the problem statement and UML to declare addGuestStudents(int) instead.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML require a method addGuestStudents(int, String) (an int plus a reason String), but the solution repository implements addGuestStudents with a single int parameter. This mismatch in the method signature (missing the reason String parameter) creates a mapping confusion: students following the specification will expect a two-parameter method but the reference implementation uses only one.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution (and template) with the problem specification: change the solution method signature to public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, String reason) and update its implementation to accept (and optionally record or log) the reason. Alternatively, if the reason parameter is intentionally unnecessary, update the problem statement and UML to specify addGuestStudents(int) to avoid confusion.
